agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

_onefetch() {
    local i cur prev opts cmd
    COMPREPLY=()
    if [[ "${BASH_VERSINFO[0]}" -ge 4 ]]; then
        cur="$2"
    else
        cur="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}"
    fi
    prev="$3"
    cmd=""
    opts=""

    for i in "${COMP_WORDS[@]:0:COMP_CWORD}"
    do
        case "${cmd},${i}" in
            ",$1")
                cmd="onefetch"
                ;;
            *)
                ;;
        esac
    done

    case "${cmd}" in
        onefetch)
            opts="-d -e -E -T -t -z -c -a -i -o -l -p -h -V --disabled-fields --no-title --number-of-authors --number-of-languages --number-of-file-churns --churn-pool-size --exclude --no-bots --no-merges --email --http-url --hide-token --include-hidden --type --text-colors --iso-time --number-separator --no-bold --ascii-input --ascii-colors --ascii-language --true-color --image --image-protocol --color-resolution --no-color-palette --no-art --nerd-fonts --output --generate --languages --package-managers --help --version [INPUT]"
            if [[ ${cur} == -* || ${COMP_CWORD} -eq 1 ]] ; then

import os, subprocess, json, shutil
BIN='/workspace/executable'
ROOT='/tmp/hx'
def setup(root=ROOT):
    if os.path.exists(root): shutil.rmtree(root)
    os.makedirs(root)
    subprocess.run(['git','init','-q','.'],cwd=root)
    subprocess.run(['git','-c','user.name=A','-c','user.email=a@x','commit','-q','--allow-empty','-m','i'],cwd=root)
def clear(root=ROOT):
    for n in os.listdir(root):
        if n=='.git': continue
        p=os.path.join(root,n)
        if os.path.isdir(p) and not os.path.islink(p): shutil.rmtree(p)
        else: os.remove(p)
def write(files, root=ROOT):
    for name,content in files.items():
        p=os.path.join(root,name)
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p),exist_ok=True)
        with open(p,'wb') as f:
            f.write(content if isinstance(content,bytes) else content.encode())
def run(extra=(), root=ROOT):
    r=subprocess.run([BIN,'-o','json','-T','programming','markup','prose','data','--number-of-languages','500']+list(extra),cwd=root,capture_output=True)
    if r.returncode!=0:
        raise Exception(r.stderr.decode())
    d=json.loads(r.stdout)
    langs=None; loc=None
    for f in d['infoFields']:
        if 'LanguagesInfo' in f: langs=[(x['language'],x['percentage']) for x in f['LanguagesInfo']['languagesWithPercentage']]
        if 'LocInfo' in f: loc=f['LocInfo']['linesOfCode']
    return langs, loc, d
def test(files, extra=(), root=ROOT):
    clear(root); write(files, root); return run(extra, root)
EOF

pub(crate) fn wrap(content: &str, hard_width: usize) -> String {
    let mut wrapper = wrap_algorithms::LineWrapper::new(hard_width);
    let mut total = Vec::new();
    for line in content.split_inclusive('\n') {
        wrapper.reset();
        let line = word_separators::find_words_ascii_space(line).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        total.extend(wrapper.wrap(line));
    }

import harness as h, json, subprocess, sys
from langmap import REP
ROOT='/tmp/hp'
h.setup(ROOT)
def run_files(files, extra=()):
    h.clear(ROOT); h.write(files, ROOT)
    r=subprocess.run([h.BIN,'-o','json','-T','programming','markup','prose','data','--number-of-languages','500']+list(extra),cwd=ROOT,capture_output=True)
    d=json.loads(r.stdout)
    langs={}; loc=0
    for f in d['infoFields']:
        if 'LanguagesInfo' in f:
            for x in f['LanguagesInfo']['languagesWithPercentage']: langs[x['language']]=x['percentage']
        if 'LocInfo' in f: loc=f['LocInfo']['linesOfCode']
    return langs, loc
def probe(content, langs=None):
    """content: str or dict lang->str. returns dict lang->code count (None if 0)."""
    langs = langs or list(REP)
    files={}
    for i,l in enumerate(langs):
        c = content[l] if isinstance(content,dict) else content
        if c is None: continue
        files['p%d.%s'%(i,REP[l])] = c
    pct, total = run_files(files)
    return {l:(round(pct[l]*total/100) if l in pct else 0) for l in langs}
EOF

//! Comment / string syntax for each supported language.

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum Family {
    None,
    Markdown,
    Rust,
    Html,
    Jupyter,
}

pub struct Syntax {
    pub line: &'static [&'static str],
    pub multi: &'static [(&'static str, &'static str)],
    pub nested_comments: &'static [(&'static str, &'static str)],
    pub allows_nested: bool,
    pub quotes: &'static [(&'static str, &'static str)],
    pub verbatim: &'static [(&'static str, &'static str)],
    pub doc: &'static [(&'static str, &'static str)],
    pub important: &'static [&'static str],
    pub fortran: bool,
    pub literate: bool,
    pub family: Family,
}

const fn base() -> Syntax {
    Syntax {
        line: &[],
        multi: &[],
        nested_comments: &[],
        allows_nested: false,
        quotes: &[],
        verbatim: &[],
        doc: &[],
        important: &[],
        fortran: false,
        literate: false,
        family: Family::None,
    }
}

const DQ: (&str, &str) = ("\"", "\"");
const SQ: (&str, &str) = ("'", "'");
const BQ: (&str, &str) = ("`", "`");
const C_BLOCK: (&str, &str) = ("/*", "*/");
const HTML_BLOCK: (&str, &str) = ("<!--", "-->");

macro_rules! syn {
    ($($field:ident : $val:expr),* $(,)?) => {
        Syntax { $($field: $val,)* ..base() }
    };
}

/// Returns the syntax of a language given its serialized (variant) name.
pub fn syntax_for(variant: &str) -> Syntax {
    match variant {
        "ABNF" => syn!(line: &[";"]),
        "Abap" => syn!(line: &["*", "\""]),
        "Ada" => syn!(line: &["--"]),
        "Agda" => syn!(line: &["--"], nested_comments: &[("{-", "-}")]),
        "Arduino" | "C" | "Cuda" | "Glsl" | "Go" | "Groovy" | "Hlsl" | "HolyC" | "Java" | "Modelica"
        | "ObjectiveC" | "Processing" | "Solidity" | "SystemVerilog" | "Verilog" => {
            syn!(line: &["//"], multi: &[C_BLOCK], quotes: &[DQ])
        }
        "Assembly" => syn!(line: &[";"], quotes: &[DQ, SQ]),
        "Ats" => syn!(line: &["//"], multi: &[("(*", "*)"), C_BLOCK], quotes: &[DQ]),
        "AutoHotKey" => syn!(line: &[";"], multi: &[C_BLOCK]),
        "Bash" | "Sh" | "Zsh" | "Fish" | "Dockerfile" | "Tcl" | "Yaml" | "Crystal" => {
            syn!(line: &["#"], quotes: &[DQ, SQ])
        }
        "CMake" => syn!(line: &["#"], quotes: &[DQ]),
        "CSharp" => syn!(line: &["//"], multi: &[C_BLOCK], quotes: &[DQ], verbatim: &[("@\"", "\"")]),
        "Ceylon" => syn!(line: &["//"], multi: &[C_BLOCK], quotes: &[DQ], verbatim: &[("\"\"\"", "\"\"\"")]),
        "Clojure" => syn!(line: &[";"], quotes: &[DQ]),
        "CoffeeScript" => syn!(line: &["#"], multi: &[("###", "###")], quotes: &[DQ, SQ]),
        "ColdFusion" => syn!(multi: &[("<!---", "--->")], quotes: &[DQ, SQ]),
        "Coq" | "OCaml" | "Wolfram" => syn!(multi: &[("(*", "*)")], quotes: &[DQ]),
        "Cpp" => syn!(line: &["//"], multi: &[C_BLOCK], quotes: &[DQ], verbatim: &[("R\"(", ")\"")]),
        "Css" | "Sass" | "Qml" | "Odin" | "OpenScad" | "Haxe" => {
            syn!(line: &["//"], multi: &[C_BLOCK], quotes: &[DQ, SQ])
        }
        "D" => syn!(line: &["//"], multi: &[C_BLOCK], nested_comments: &[("/+", "+/")], quotes: &[DQ, SQ]),
